# Mochi2D

> Mochi2D is an open-source runtime for models made with Live2D Cubism: a from-scratch TypeScript runtime and WebGL renderer for `.moc3` files with `model3.json`, motions, expressions, physics, pose, eye blink, breath, look, lip sync and motion sync. AI agents drive it through an MCP server (`mochi2d-mcp`, stdio) or a headless command line (`mochi2d`) with the same operations.

- 0.19.0 is a 1.0 candidate: every export is marked stable or experimental (docs/api-stability.md), docs/versioning.md says what releases may change, and docs/migration.md lists renames and removals since 0.10.0 (the 0.16.0 aliases are gone: use `sourceFromFolder`, `sourceFromZipFile`, `NodeFileSource`, `BrowserFileSource`, `SettingsFormatError`, `MochiHitEvent.areas`).
- Build with `npm ci && npm run build` (Node ≥ 20). The MCP server is `dist/tools/mochi2d-mcp.js` and the command line is `dist/tools/mochi2d.js`; in the repository folder, `npx mochi2d-mcp --root <folder>` and `npx mochi2d <command>` run them.
- The MCP server reads files only under the folders given with `--root`, `MOCHI2D_ROOTS` or the client's roots. It writes nothing and makes no network requests.
- MCP tools: `list_models`, `load_model`, `describe_model`, `get_parameters`, `set_parameters`, `get_part_opacities`, `set_part_opacities`, `play_expression`, `play_motion`, `play_sound`, `advance_time`, `reset`, `render` (returns a PNG image), `hit_test`, `map_points`, `validate_moc3`. Resources: `mochi2d://model` and the docs.
- A typical session: `list_models`, `load_model`, `describe_model`, then `set_parameters` or `play_motion` with `advance_time`, then `render` to look at the result.
- While physics runs, it overwrites some parameters (DeepSeek-chan's `ParamAngleX` follows `AngleX`): set one of the `physicsInputs` that `describe_model` lists for them instead; `set_parameters` says so in `physicsOverwrites`.
- `play_expression` with `mode: "add"` shows several expressions at once; `play_motion` with `hold: true` keeps the last frame (eye blink resumes at its end unless `blinkWhileHeld: false`); `map_points` maps points through a deformer at the current pose, with Jacobians; `advance_time` reports each motion's end and its reason.
- Motion sync (`.motionsync3.json`): `play_sound` moves the mouth with a WAV file through a setting of the model's motion-sync file, and a motion whose settings entry links a `Sound` and a `MotionSync` setting does the same; `advance_time` then reports how often each element (`Silence`, `A`, `I`, `U`, `E`, `O`) was the strongest and the latest weights. Mochi2D reads the file and its settings, and analyses the audio with its own method, so its mouth shapes are its own.
- Rendering needs headless Chromium through Playwright; everything else works without it. `render` with `maxTextureSize` is a faster preview, not the reference render.
- Coordinates are in model units, x to the right and y up; `describe_model` gives the canvas size.
- Evaluation (vertices, opacities, colors) uses a fixed float32 order of operations; in the project's tests, static results on the conformance catalog are bit-identical with the official runtime's (docs/conformance.md).
- Reference renders (`npm run render`, `NodeRenderer`, `renderToPng`) use the float32 rules of docs/rendering.md; in the project's tests on SwiftShader, all 53 catalog renders are pixel-identical with the official renderer's (docs/conformance.md).
- The library has four entry points: `mochi2d` (browsers, `MochiView`, plus `readMoc`, `writeMoc`, `mocModelFromData`, `parsePhysics`, `writePhysics`, `parseMotionSync` and `writeMotionSync`), `mochi2d/headless` (`ModelRuntime`, `MemoryFileSource`, `mocModelFromData`, the same file readers and writers), `mochi2d/node` (`loadModelFromDisk`, and `NodeRenderer` for PNG renders with Playwright as an optional peer) and `mochi2d/pixi` (`MochiSprite`, a PixiJS v8 display object: `await MochiSprite.from(url, { renderer: app.renderer, ticker: app.ticker })`, then `app.stage.addChild(sprite)` and `sprite.model` for the model API; PixiJS 8.12 or later as an optional peer).
- For live apps: `model.setTint(meshId, [r, g, b, a])` tints art meshes (r, g, b up to 2 to brighten toward white; in views, items and `NodeRenderer` renders); `model.updateTexture(index, image, { x, y })` replaces a texture or a region of it in place (straight-alpha RGBA, an ImageBitmap or a canvas), drawn from the next frame; `model.setIdleWeight(id, 0)` keeps the idle animation off a parameter that tracking writes with `setParameter`; `item.mirror` flips an item model (its forwarded `ParamAngleX` and `ParamAngleZ` negated, so it turns with the main model); `model.setPhysicsStrength(k)`, `setPhysicsSettingStrength(id, k)`, `setPhysicsWind(x, y)` and `setPhysicsSettingWind(id, multiplier)` (how much of the wind one setting feels; 1 is the reference, 0 shields it) change physics at runtime (strength 1 is the reference; views hold physics while paused, `holdPhysicsWhenPaused`); `getParameterBase(id)` reads the base value beside `getParameter(id)`, the drawn value (`get_parameters` reports both, as `base` and `value`); `model.speak(audio, { motionSync: true })` and `model.startLiveMotionSync()` (microphone or a `MediaStream`, without the browser's voice processing unless `voiceProcessing: true`) drive the mouth by motion sync, `model.motionSync` gives the element weights and the level at every analysis, and `VoiceCalibration` with `view.recordAudio(seconds)` makes a voice profile to save and load; `item.layer = { above: meshId }` (or `below`) draws an item between the main model's art meshes, and `item.split = { mesh, back }` draws it in two parts, each at its own place; `model.setPhysicsRate(stepsPerSecond)` changes the physics rate.
- Expression calls take fade times that replace the file's: `model.setExpression(name, { fadeIn, fadeOut })`, `addExpression(name, { fadeIn, fadeOut })`, `removeExpression(name, { fadeOut })` and `clearExpression({ fadeOut })`, in seconds.
- Editors change a shown model without reloading it: `model.patch(...)` writes new keyform positions, opacities, draw orders, colors, rotation values and glue values in place, and `model.replace(mocBytes | MocData, version)` shows other data keeping the textures, the view and the parameter values. For a timeline with physics, `model.savePhysicsState()` and `restorePhysicsState(state)` continue the physics from a saved frame bit for bit; `writePhysics(data)` writes physics data back to `.physics3.json`, and `writeMotionSync(data)` motion-sync settings to `.motionsync3.json`.
- A view nobody sees can keep its model moving without drawing: `view.drawing = false` (or `view.advance(seconds, { draw: false })` in your own loop) advances motions, events, expressions, physics, live lip sync and items; `view.draw()` draws the current state, the same picture as drawing every frame.

## Docs

- [Agent API](docs/agent-api.md): the MCP server's tools and resources, the command line, safety, rendering requirements and MCP client configurations
- [Library API](docs/api.md): `MochiView`, `MochiSprite` (PixiJS), `ModelRuntime`, `loadModelFromDisk`, `NodeRenderer`, items (between the main model's art meshes, split items), lip sync, motion sync and voice calibration, motion ends, physics inputs, physics strength, wind, rate and state, physics and motion-sync files, base values, idle weights, tints, editing a shown model
- [API stability](docs/api-stability.md): every export of the four entry points, marked stable or experimental
- [Versioning](docs/versioning.md): what major, minor and patch releases may change (exports, results bit-exact with the official runtime, renders, file formats, deprecation)
- [Migration from 0.x](docs/migration.md): every rename and removal since 0.10.0, and behavior changes that may need code changes
- [Model data](docs/moc-data.md): `MocData`, `readMoc`, `writeMoc`, `validateMoc` and `mocModelFromData` for reading, writing, validating and previewing `.moc3` files
- [Viewer guide](docs/viewer.md): the web viewer (menus, resource tree, settings, tools for checking a model, editing motion settings, expressions and poses, new expressions) and its static build
- [Architecture](docs/architecture.md): how the parts of Mochi2D fit together
- [Rendering rules](docs/rendering.md): the float32 rules of Mochi2D's reference renders (texture v, mask matrices, layer reads, masked layers through the inverse view matrix)
